newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore noon shares softer on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Singapore noon shares softer on profit taking.

text.p: Singapore shares adopted a softer posture at midday on Wednesday succumbing to some profit taking on blue chip and electronic stocks.
Earlier momentum from an overnight rally in Wall Street was not sustained partly because institutional interest was subdued.
"There are no major buy programs, only recommendations of stocks that might have fallen recently," a bank dealer said.
At the lunchtime break, the Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) was down 1.75 points at 2,045.81.
Volume was a modest 81 million shares with advancers beating losers 210 to 71.
Malaysian over-the-counter issues and small-capitalisation stocks in Singapore received moderate interest from retail investors, but the mood was also cautious, dealers said.

Among actives, SM Summit traded up Singapore four cents to S$1.06, fanned by speculation over how it would place 10 million new shares. Singapore Telecom also attracted demand, falling to a new low of S$2.60, but paring losses at midday to stand at S$2.65 on a volume of 4.1 million shares.
Foreign tranches were among the top gainers, including UOB, up Singapore 30 cents to S$14.90, OCBC up 20 cents at S$17.80 and SIA up 20 cents to S$12.30. -- Jacqueline Wong (65 8703080)
